statements.statement: A 100W lightbulb uses more total energy than a 10W lightbulb no matter what.
statements.explanation: Power measures the rate of energy use, not total energy. A 10W bulb left on for 100 hours uses more total energy than a 100W bulb on for 5 minutes. Total energy depends on both power and time.

statements.statement: One watt equals one joule of energy consumed per second.
statements.explanation: By definition, 1 watt = 1 joule/second. Watts measure how quickly energy is being used.

statements.statement: A device with a higher wattage rating consumes energy at a faster rate.
statements.explanation: Higher watts means more joules used per second, so yes, energy is consumed more quickly.
Power is measured in watts (W). Volts measure voltage, which is electrical pressure -- a different quantity entirely.
